original_test_intent: Prove that the HMC-owned logical I2C-7 path reaches the physically populated second HPM in the required 2P configuration and can independently identify its HPM1 devices, without accepting responses from HPM0 or a similarly numbered BMC bus.
original_method: Establish HMC ownership or documented BMC proxy for logical I2C-7; prove 2P/HPM1 population; bind the HMC controller/access endpoint, adapter, mux/channel and second-HPM connector; define HPM1-specific device addresses and read-safe identity registers/values distinct from HPM0; have an operator inspect/photograph the physical HMC-HPM1 path; preserve management/bus logs; use only allowlisted read-only operations; retain complete second-HPM responses and stop on wrong-path, bus or management faults without write/reset/retry.
manual_activity: An operator proves the 2P configuration, inspects the HMC-to-second-HPM connector/cable and supplies HPM1-bound photos; the owner identifies the authoritative HMC access endpoint.
required_inputs: HMC/BMC ownership diagram and native HMC or explicitly mapped proxy access for logical HMC I2C-7
Approved 2P population and HMC controller/adapter/mux/channel/second-HPM connector map
HPM1-specific 7-bit device addresses, read-safe identity registers/masks/values and HPM0 distinction
Physical procedure, prohibited transactions, management/bus error limits, aborts and recovery
safety_requirements: Use only the authoritative HMC path or documented proxy and select the verified HPM1 channel
Do not accept HPM0 or independent BMC responses as second-HPM evidence
Never quick-write, scan unknown devices, write EEPROM/control registers or service a live connector without approval
Stop on wrong-path response, missing/unexpected device, timeout, stuck bus, arbitration storm or HMC/BMC instability
agent_execution_scope: Validate ownership/proxy, 2P state, HPM1 topology, identity oracle and safe command allowlist
After physical confirmation, collect HMC-path read-only HPM1 identity and bus-health evidence
Prove second-HPM selection and compare every response with the HPM1-specific oracle
Do not guess access surface, substitute HPM0/BMC data, probe unknown addresses, perform writes, reset controllers or issue the DUT verdict
engineer_actions: Approve HMC versus BMC ownership/proxy, 2P/HPM1 population and exact I2C-7 mux/connector path
Approve HPM1-specific devices/registers/values, safe commands, physical evidence, error limits and recovery
Review physical and target-bound communication evidence and decide PASS, FAIL, or BLOCKED

command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use the owner-approved HMC-native or mapped proxy method on the exact second-HPM channel and query only the HPM1 identity allowlist, preserving path-selection and bus-health evidence.

modernized_recommendation.status: MEDIUM HMC-OWNERSHIP-BOUND SECOND-HPM PHYSICAL AND I2C FUNCTIONAL CHECK
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Prove 2P population and HMC control path, select the exact HPM1 mux channel, then combine operator physical evidence with a second-HPM-specific read-only identity oracle.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds HMC/BMC disambiguation, 2P/HPM1 proof, wrong-HPM exclusion, safe identity evidence and recovery.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: The same addresses behind HPM0 and HPM1 muxes can yield a plausible map from the wrong HPM, while a similarly numbered BMC bus may be physically unrelated.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Proxied management access and live mux state are platform-specific; generic scans can disturb devices or switch away from the intended second-HPM path.

review_improvement: Prevents first-HPM or unrelated BMC evidence from falsely passing the HMC second-HPM case and adds safe, path-bound HPM1 identity plus physical proof.
independent_technical_reasoning: This row's distinguishing coverage is HPM1 in a 2P configuration. Repeated address maps behind separate mux channels make unbound scan output especially misleading, and HMC/BMC bus names are not interchangeable. Therefore proof must jointly establish controller ownership, second-HPM channel selection, HPM1-specific identities and physical population. Only allowlisted reads are safe because generic discovery can issue transactions unsupported by live VR or EEPROM devices.
